structure.heading: Regulatory Obligation-to-Control Coverage and Compliance Posture (as of 2026-05-01)
text_content: **Regulatory Obligation-to-Control Coverage and Compliance Posture (as of 2026-05-01)**

As of 2026-05-01, 42 of 48 regulatory obligations are mapped to internal controls, representing 87.5% coverage. The control mapping inventory is maintained in the GRC platform and is updated weekly; unmapped obligations are prioritized for mapping during the May–June control identification sprint. Control owners and process leads receive monthly exceptions reports to validate mappings and governance documentation updates.

Eleven obligations are rated High risk impact; notable among these is the GLBA Safeguards Rule, 16 CFR Part 314, which is included in the high-risk inventory for enhanced monitoring. Remediation resources are allocated to these 11 items with weekly status reviews, risk owners assignde, and a targeted escalation path to the Chief Compliance Officer for any schedule slippage.

structure.heading: Examination Findings and Remediation Plan Tracking with Target Closure Dates
text_content: **Examination Findings and Remediation Plan Tracking with Target Closure Dates**

There are currently nine open examination findings arising from three examinations: OCC 2026-02, CFPB 2026-03, and State AG 2026-04. As of 2026-05-01, four of these nine findings are past due, representing 44.4% (4 of 9) of the open population. The remaining five findings remain within their planned remediation windows. Each finding is logged with a unique identifier, assigned remediation owner, mapped internal control(s), and documented root-cause analysis. This baseline count establishes the scope for targeted remediation tracking and regulatory reporting through the remainder of 2026 period.

OCC-2026-02-F-03 is the highest-severity open finding and has a target closure date of 2026-05-31. This item is prioritized for immediate executive attention given its severity rating, impact to capital and consumer compliance controls, and the regulatory profile of the OCC. The remediation plan allocates dedicated remediation leads, vendor support where required, and a test-and-validate phase scheduled the week prior to the target date. With 30 days to target as of 2026-05-01, escalation protocols and contingency resources are prepositioned to mitigate the risk of regulatory enforcement actions.
